identity.name: Grand Complications Chronograph
identity.one_liner: The first Patek chronograph with the in-house CH 29-535 PS caliber (2010), in yellow gold. The textbook manual-wind dress chronograph of the 2010s.

narrative.story: The 5170J is the reference that retired the Lemania-derived caliber that Patek had used for fifty years. The CH 29-535 PS is the first chronograph caliber fully designed in-house, and it is also the first with a column wheel visible through the case back. The 5170 family (J yellow, R rose, G white) ran 2010-2018 before the 5172 replaced it. The 5170 is the last of the manually-wound Patek dress chronographs; the 5172 added a pulsometer scale.
narrative.collector_notes: The CH 29-535 PS has six patents on the chronograph mechanism alone, including the tooth profile of the column wheel. The 5170 is the reference a collector cites when they want to argue Patek's chronograph chronograph engineering is real, not decorative.
